header: The hospital route (step 51a): I answer questions about the OPD from the hospital data, deterministically and without a model call. It runs right after the holiday parser in the omnibar. When a question is not clearly about the hospital OPD I return null and let the other routes go on. What it understands today (I add more together with the data):
- is the OPD open today / tomorrow / on a weekday / on a date (and why not) - which days a doctor sits in the OPD, and whether he sits on a date
- who is in a department's OPD on a weekday / date - a unit (OPD number, or "unit 2" of a department) with its days and head
- a department's OPD at a glance - the head of a unit and the HOD of a department
- OPD and token timings - the days the OPD is closed

For the HOD and the unit heads I follow the usual rule at the hospital: the first-named doctor of a unit is its head, and one of the unit heads is the HOD (set in the data when known). The hospital's lists are out of date, so I MARK a doctor who has retired or is not on the current doctor list and never show him silently as sitting.

symbols.name: DeptDoctor
doc: "list of ent doctors", "how many doctors in surgery": the HR directory does not know a doctor's hospital department (all 52 are in MEDICAL ORGANISATION), so the SQL could only answer 0 rows, or silently ignore the department. So I use the hospital's own lists, which know it: the staff list (department of each doctor), the OPD schedule (who sits in the department's OPD) and the list of the non-permanent doctors. For me a doctor of a department is one whose staff-list department it is, or who sits in its OPD, or a non-permanent doctor whose department or specialization it is. I do not list a doctor who has retired or been transferred.

symbols.name: SPECIALISATION_WORD
doc: "the specialisation of doctors in dsp" (26 Oct 2026: the search answered with an unrelated circular at 87 per cent). A degree or qualification is any of MBBS, MD, MS ...; in my rule a SPECIALISATION comes only from a POSTGRADUATE qualification: MD, MS, DNB, DrNB, MCh, DM, MDS, or a postgraduate diploma (DGO, DPM, DIH, D.Ortho) or MRCOG. A doctor with MBBS alone has none; one whose qualification is not recorded is not known; one whose postgraduate qualification names no subject (a bare "MS") has a specialisation that is not stated, and I never guess it from the department.

symbols.name: openGate
symbols.sig: async function openGate(e: Entities, ctx: EngineCtx)
doc: An open OPD is not yet an answer for a person: it depends on the DEPARTMENT he wants to visit and, for a department of units, on the UNIT he already belongs to (a patient is seen only by the unit of his first visit; a new patient belongs to the unit that sits on the day of the first visit). So I give a vague question about an open day a soft, amber first answer and a short question-and-answer: which department? then, for Medicine, which unit (or "new patient")? Only then do I give the clear Yes or No. A closed day, or today out of hours, is a clear No at once.
